You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like late 2011, most likely September or October.

- **Labor and rates:** unemployment of 9.0% and a fed funds rate of 0.08% fit 2011. The 10-year yield at 2.00% fits late 2011, and so does the 20y+ Treasury 6-month return of +24.9%.
- **Inflation:** headline CPI of 3.56% YoY fits September 2011, when it was 3.9%. August was 3.8% and October 3.5%. Core CPI at 2.1% fits October 2011, when it was about 2.1%. Core CPI in September was 2.0%.
- **Unemployment:** it was 9.0% in October 2011 (9.1% in September), and the 3-month change of -0.1 fits.
- **Payrolls:** the 3-month average of 114k fits October 2011.
- **Markets:** the VIX at 30.64 is near the end of September 2011 (VIX 42.96) or October (VIX 29.96 at the October close). The 10-year yield was about 1.98% at the end of October 2011, which fits. The 1-month US equity return of -0.4% does not fit October, which was strongly positive at about +11%.
- **Month-end data:** September 2011 had the 10-year at 1.92% and large-cap equity -7%. The 1-month investment-grade credit return of -3.2% fits September 2011 (long credit fell), but the US equity figure is off for that month too. The 10-year yield 3-month change of -0.23 fits November 2011 (2.07%) or December 2011 (1.88%), while the 12m change of -0.81 fits roughly 2.8% a year earlier.
- **Choosing the month:** November 2011 had equity at -0.2%, a VIX of 27.8, and developed ex-US at -2.2%, which fits well. The 10-year yield was 2.0% at the end of November and the 2-year was 0.25%. Core CPI was 2.2% in November. Payrolls averaged about 114k over the previous three months, and unemployment was 8.6% in November, so that part does not fit. The unemployment figure may have been the originally published 9.0% from the October report, and the VIX of 30.64 matches the November 30 close of about 27.8 only roughly. I pick November 2011.
